title: Aviation mechanic major alterations, major repairs and preventive maintenance practice questions
description: Practice questions on 14 CFR Part 43 Appendix A: what makes an alteration or repair major, and the conditions on preventive maintenance items.

questions.question: Part 43 applies to aircraft issued a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category, with some exceptions. For which products does 43.1(d)(3) say the listing of major alterations and major repairs in paragraphs (a) and (b) of appendix A is not applicable?

options.A: Products maintained only by their owner
options.B: Products not produced under an FAA approval
options.C: Products more than 20 years old
options.D: Products used only for flight training

questions.explanation: 43.1(d)(3) states: "The listing of major alterations and major repairs specified in paragraphs (a) and (b) of appendix A of this part is not applicable to products not produced under an FAA approval."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The listing of major alterations and major repairs specified in paragraphs (a) and (b) of appendix A of this part is not applicable to products not produced under an FAA approval.

questions.question: Appendix A, paragraph (a)(1), names parts and types of alterations of an airframe. Under what condition are those alterations airframe major alterations?

options.A: When they are performed by someone other than the manufacturer
options.B: When they take more than one day to complete
options.C: When they are done on an aircraft used for hire
options.D: When not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(1) states that alterations of the listed parts and types, "when not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA, are airframe major alterations."

questions.question: An owner plans a change to the aircraft's empty weight and empty balance. Under Appendix A (a)(1)(xi), such changes are airframe major alterations when they result in what?

options.A: An increase in the maximum certificated weight or center of gravity limits of the aircraft
options.B: Any change of the empty weight, however small
options.C: A change that needs a new equipment list
options.D: A reduction of the aircraft's useful load

questions.explanation: Item (a)(1)(xi) reads: "Changes to the empty weight or empty balance which result in an increase in the maximum certificated weight or center of gravity limits of the aircraft."

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(1)(xiii), changes to the wing or to fixed or movable control surfaces are listed as airframe major alterations when they affect which characteristics?

options.A: Paint and finish characteristics
options.B: Stall warning characteristics
options.C: Flutter and vibration characteristics
options.D: Ground handling characteristics

questions.explanation: Item (a)(1)(xiii) reads: "Changes to the wing or to fixed or movable control surfaces which affect flutter and vibration characteristics."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A—Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Appendix A (a)(2)(i) lists the conversion of an aircraft engine from one approved model to another as a powerplant major alteration when the conversion involves what?

options.A: Any changes in compression ratio, propeller reduction gear, impeller gear ratios or the substitution of major engine parts which requires extensive rework and testing of the engine
options.B: Any change of the engine's data plate, even with no change to its parts
options.C: Only a change of the engine's paint or finish
options.D: Only a change made by a person other than the engine manufacturer

questions.explanation: Item (a)(2)(i) covers a conversion "involving any changes in compression ratio, propeller reduction gear, impeller gear ratios or the substitution of major engine parts which requires extensive rework and testing of the engine."

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(2)(ii), changes to the engine by replacing aircraft engine structural parts are a powerplant major alteration when the replacement parts are which?

options.A: Parts bought from a different parts distributor
options.B: Parts not supplied by the original manufacturer or parts not specifically approved by the Administrator
options.C: Parts that are new rather than overhauled
options.D: Parts installed by the holder of a powerplant rating

questions.explanation: Item (a)(2)(ii) reads: "Changes to the engine by replacing aircraft engine structural parts with parts not supplied by the original manufacturer or parts not specifically approved by the Administrator."

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(3), when are the listed alterations of a propeller propeller major alterations?

options.A: When the propeller has more than two blades
options.B: When the propeller is removed from the aircraft for the work
options.C: When the work is done by a repair station
options.D: When not authorized in the propeller specifications issued by the FAA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(3) states: "The following alterations of a propeller when not authorized in the propeller specifications issued by the FAA are propeller major alterations".

questions.question: Under Appendix A (a)(4), which alterations of an appliance's basic design are appliance major alterations?

options.A: Any alteration of the basic design, however it is made
options.B: Only alterations requested by the aircraft owner
options.C: Alterations of the basic design not made in accordance with recommendations of the appliance manufacturer or in accordance with an FAA Airworthiness Directive
options.D: Only alterations that add weight to the appliance

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(4) states: "Alterations of the basic design not made in accordance with recommendations of the appliance manufacturer or in accordance with an FAA Airworthiness Directive are appliance major alterations."

questions.question: Appendix A (a)(4) also covers radio communication and navigation equipment approved under type certification or a Technical Standard Order. Which changes in the basic design of that equipment are also major alterations?

options.A: Only changes that replace the equipment's display
options.B: Only changes made outside the equipment manufacturer's facility
options.C: Only changes that require new wiring in the aircraft
options.D: Changes that have an effect on frequency stability, noise level, sensitivity, selectivity, distortion, spurious radiation, AVC characteristics, or ability to meet environmental test conditions, and other changes that have an effect on the performance of the equipment

questions.explanation: The appendix covers changes to such equipment "that have an effect on frequency stability, noise level, sensitivity, selectivity, distortion, spurious radiation, AVC characteristics, or ability to meet environmental test conditions and other changes that have an effect on the performance of the equipment are also major alterations."

questions.question: Appendix A (b)(1) lists parts and types of repairs of an airframe. What must those repairs involve to be airframe major repairs?

options.D: Only repairs made after an accident reported to the FAA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (b)(1) covers repairs "involving the strengthening, reinforcing, splicing, and manufacturing of primary structural members or their replacement, when replacement is by fabrication such as riveting or welding, are airframe major repairs."

options.C: A carburetor of any type
